title: Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models
domain: language modelling (few-shot word-mapping tasks, in-context learning)
tasks_benchmarks: camelCase, Roman numerals, SST-2, word length, last letter, Pig Latin (7B/14B)

headline_result.text: With 16 examples, 50 forward passes and no gradients, finished editor runs reach 88.5-93.0% zero-shot accuracy on Qwen2.5-0.5B versus 89.3% for 16-shot ICL and 86.5-88.2% for Adam/LoRA/rank-1/context-distillation fine-tuning on the same pairs, while changing far fewer weights (8,512 for Fable 5.1); the authors conclude WSP adds legibility, not accuracy.
headline_result.quote: In our study, weight-space ... programming adds legibility, not accuracy.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3 data splits (one run per split) on Qwen2.5-0.5B; single split for scale, family and most appendix conditions

key_claims.claim: Finished editor updates reach 88.5% (Fable 5.1) and 90.4% (Opus 5.5) mean zero-shot accuracy on Qwen2.5-0.5B against 89.3% for 16-shot ICL, from a 0-3% unedited baseline.
key_claims.quote: updates reach a mean of 88.5% (Fable 5.1) and ... 90.4% (Opus 5.5) against 89.3% for 16-shot ICL

key_claims.claim: Gradient fine-tuning on the same 16 pairs, with hyperparameters chosen on 30 dev items, reaches 86.5% (Adam), 88.0% (context distillation), 87.9% (LoRA) and 88.2% (matched rank-1), the rank-1 update changing 4,358,143 entries versus 8,512 for Fable 5.1; no editor-baseline difference survives multiple-comparison correction.

limitations_stated.text: The main study uses one model family; scale, family and hybrid conditions use a single split, so few-point differences are within split noise.
limitations_stated.quote: Scope of the evidence. The main study uses one ... model family, Qwen2.5;

limitations_stated.text: The editor kernel was not sandboxed (internet-connected node, harness process); an unconfined open-weight editor did read the test split.

limitations_stated.text: The 50-forward-pass budget is not binding for every editor because Gemini 4 Argon re-implemented the model on CPU to evaluate candidates.
limitations_stated.quote: since Gemini 4 Argon evaluated candidate updates ... through a CPU re-implementation of the model;

notes_for_review: The most careful WSP-vs-fine-tuning comparison so far: four frontier editors, scripted task-vector baselines, a norm- and sparsity-matched random-edit control, and Adam/LoRA/rank-1/context-distillation baselines on the same 16 pairs over three splits, with paired bootstrap and Holm-corrected sign-flip tests. Budgets are asymmetric: editors get 50 forward passes, 80-150 turns and no dev data, while gradient baselines tune learning rate, steps and rank on 30 dev items; editors also bring task knowledge (typed pairs covering 0-98% of hidden test inputs), which explains part of their parity, and unfinished runs are excluded from the headline means. Cost is about $779 for 224 runs (about $1 per GPT-6 Astra run); code is promised but not yet released.
